dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Listed network sizes, inspected the reference alignment, and analyzed graph stats (degree distribution) — systematic per-pair characterization of the concrete instances.
Scored the reference alignment's S3, quantifying what a strong reference achieves — establishing a baseline/ceiling before committing.

Checked compilers/cores (runtime feasibility), then selected and implemented SANA, a known published simulated-annealing network aligner well-suited to S3 optimization — a concrete method with clear fit rationale.

Separated the S3 vs NC levers: pure-S3 run to observe 'natural NC' vs sweeping NC weights seeded from the reference alignment — recognizing topology drives S3 while reference-seeding drives NC, and that the two deliverables have different constraints.
Returned to degree statistics mid-run, showing sustained structural characterization rather than one-off inspection.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond the level-5 anchor: it characterized each network pair by size and degree distribution, inspected AND scored the reference alignment to quantify a baseline, checked runtime constraints, and selected a specific published method (SANA) tuned to S3. It also explicitly identified the task-specific levers — topology for S3, reference-seeding for NC, with differing per-deliverable constraints — matching the level-8 description. It does not reach 10 because there is no visible evaluation of multiple competing published methods against the instance sizes; SANA was adopted directly.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Ordered setup sub-goals: list networks/sizes, inspect reference alignment, analyze graph stats, score reference S3, check compilers — establishing problem structure before acting.

Scored reference alignment and independently scored a test run BEFORE optimizing — scorer/metric built and verified prior to optimization, a sensibly sequenced milestone with a numeric (threshold) done-check.
Two deliverables handled distinctly: yeast via NC-weight sweeps seeded from the reference (to meet the NC constraint), DM-HS via separate pure-S3 runs (S3-only goal).
Baseline install milestones ('install yeast alignment', 'install DM-HS baseline') before refinement chains — baseline-measured then optimize structure.
Much larger optimization budget spent on the harder fly S3 task (launch_dm..dm8, repeated kill/relaunch as fallback branches) vs. yeast finalized earlier — effort budgeted by difficulty.
Explicit gating/done-checks near the end: 'reconfirm yeast deliverable', 'reconfirm both', strict format validation — checking measured scores/format before declaring done.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation and tracks both deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals (well above anchor 5). The action arc — stats → score reference/metric computable → baseline measured → optimize to threshold → reconfirm/validate — is sequenced sensibly (scorer built and validated before optimizing) and shows difficulty-aware effort budgeting toward the harder fly S3 task with kill/relaunch fallback branches, matching much of anchor 8 and touching anchor 10. It falls short of a clean 8+ because the milestones are observable in the behavior rather than articulated as an explicit hierarchy with stated numeric done-criteria per stage.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Scores the provided reference alignment for S3 — the canonical sanity-check that the scorer produces sensible values on a known-good input (level-8 behavior).
'Independently score test output' — maintains a local scorer separate from the aligner's own reported objective, cross-checking rather than trusting the tool's number.
Builds a scoring script over all outputs, catches and fixes a bug ('Fix and rerun scoring'), then does a 'Clean scoring of all four' — demonstrates scrutiny of the scorer itself.
'Independently score DM-HS outputs' — same independent verification applied to the second deliverable, used as the pass/fail gate before install.
'Validate file formats strictly' — exact node-name/format/coverage checking against the spec before finalizing submission.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent builds and repeatedly uses an independent S3/NC scorer as its optimization/stopping objective (steps 25, 267, 443), sanity-checks it against the provided reference alignment (step 12), catches and fixes a bug in the scorer itself (steps 269-272), and strictly validates output format against the spec (step 489). This matches the level-8 anchor's faithful, sanity-checked scorer used as the feedback loop; it edges toward but doesn't clearly reach the level-10 bar of explicit double-counting/off-by-one guarding, and the index carries no observation text to confirm formula faithfulness, so I hold at 8 with medium confidence.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Scores reference alignment S3 to establish a baseline, and runs an explicit 'Pareto sweep + ceiling test' — measuring distance to the achievable ceiling, showing awareness of where current scores sit relative to targets/max.
Repeatedly and independently scores its own outputs (S3/NC) rather than trusting solver logs, giving continuity of measured results across variants.

Explicitly preserves best-so-far per deliverable ('Save best DM', 'Install yeast alignment', 'Install DM-HS baseline', 'Install final DM-HS and reconfirm both') while continuing to explore — hallmark of not losing the plot over a long run.
Kills stalled/unproductive runs (sana2, f-runs, k-runs, m-runs) and launches new variants (dm2→dm8), indicating recognition that an approach stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
Extensive, sustained progress-checking across every long run maintains a running picture of convergence, though many are polling-style status checks rather than logged score progression.

dimensions.reasoning: The action descriptions show the agent consistently measures scores (independent S3/NC scoring), preserves and reinstalls best-so-far alignments per deliverable, runs ceiling/Pareto tests to gauge distance to targets, and repeatedly kills plateaued variants to try new approaches instead of looping — squarely the level-8 profile of best-so-far tracking with plateau/regression recognition. It nudges toward level 10 (ceiling test, reconfirm-both at the end) but I cannot confirm true numeric score-progression logging from titles alone, and much of the monitoring is polling-style, so I hold at 8.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: After a pure-S3 run to 'observe natural NC', pivots to 'Sweep NC weights seeded from reference' — diagnoses NC shortfall and switches to reference-seeding + NC-weight objective, a materially different signal targeted at the lagging metric.
Edits objective to CAP NC (only 0.30 required) so S3 isn't sacrificed — deliberate, diagnosis-driven objective tuning distinguishing the two constraints.
Progression through materially different tactics for DM-HS (guided moves, degree seeding, best-of-k, refinement chains) each prompted by prior results — repeated strategy revision, not seed reruns.
Repeatedly kills unproductive run families (reheats, best-of-k, productive-band), abandoning dead ends quickly.
Installs/saves best-so-far and builds refinement chains from installed baselines — keeps accumulated gains rather than discarding when pivoting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent handles the two distinct constraint sets (DM-HS S3-only vs. yeast S3+NC) with different signals, explicitly diagnoses the NC shortfall and responds with reference-seeding then NC-capping (steps 34-41, 245-247), cycles through many materially different topological/seeding tactics, and abandons dead ends while preserving best-so-far baselines. This is well past the anchor-8 'diagnose and pivot deliberately, keeping what worked' and approaches anchor-10 fluid, evidence-driven correction combining complementary signals. I land at 9 rather than 10 given the evidence is step-title level, limiting visibility into the depth of the hypotheses.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
